drafted_from: tool:keep-a-local-file-in-my-files's row in tools/sync-files-between-my-computers/tool-rows.json, do-work/keep-a-local-file.mjs and test/keep-a-local-file.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep /tmp/shoot/clip.mp4 on this computer in my Files as /site/clip.mp4, type video/mp4." It runs tool:keep-a-local-file-in-my-files, which reads the file in place and answers what was kept and what was refused.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes file paths and names as input and writes the files themselves into the person's Files.
instructions: 1. Pick the regular files on your computer to keep (full path each, not a link or folder) and the absolute name each gets in Files, such as /site/clip.mp4 (letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; folders by slash).

2. Say to your AI: "Keep these files in my Files" and give the paths and names. For one file the input is {path, name, media_type}; for several it is {files: [{path, name, media_type}, ...]}, at most 256.
3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:keep-a-local-file-in-my-files (the worked example shows the call).

4. Read the answer: kept lists each file's name, bytes, media_type and the door's finish; refused names each file that was not kept with its reason. One refusal does not stop the others. Fix those names or paths and run again for only them.

worked_examples.title: Keep one 100,000-byte video in Files as /site/clip.mp4
worked_examples.given: From tools/sync-files-between-my-computers/test/keep-a-local-file.test.mjs ('keeps a regular file in pieces'): a regular file of 100000 bytes, below the whole-file threshold, so it is sent in pieces (a write_file_start, at least two write_file_piece, then a write_file_finish).

worked_examples.title: A link and a bad name are refused while the good file is kept
worked_examples.ask: Keep these three files in my Files.
worked_examples.given: From tools/sync-files-between-my-computers/test/keep-a-local-file.test.mjs ('a list keeps each file in order and names each refusal'): /tmp/shoot/link.txt is a symbolic link to /tmp/shoot/real.txt, which is a 1-byte regular file. Read from do-work/keep-a-local-file.mjs for the exact words and the bytes.
